info: Keep logging food in Lose It! This screen reads available Health Connect nutrition alongside any food already logged in Pulse. Lose It! takes priority, then MyFitnessPal; other nutrition origins are fallbacks, never added on top. Expenditure is an open, experimental estimate from intake and weigh-ins, not MacroFactor’s proprietary algorithm. Fitbit activity remains a separate comparison and never adds calories to your food budget. Everything here is calculated on this phone without an AI service.
source: Keep logging in Lose It! · sync through Health Connect
partialDayA11y: {{day}}: {{eaten}} kcal logged. Incomplete food log, excluded from estimates. Current target {{target}} kcal.
referenceOnly: Reference only · set your own calorie target
calibrationNote: Needs at least 14 consecutive days of calorie logs and 7 weigh-ins spanning that interval. Missing food is never assumed to be zero.
assumption: A calorie total does not prove that every meal was logged. The model assumes complete food logs and consistent weigh-in timing. Water changes and logging errors can both change the estimate.
dayNotFinished: A daily deficit appears after the day ends, with usable intake and expenditure data.
partialHint: Turns on automatically when entries are missing calories. Turn it off to confirm the known day total and include it in charts and estimates. Your choice is saved for this day, including after sync, without changing Lose It! or Health Connect.
missingEnergy: Marked incomplete automatically: some entries are missing calories. Turn the switch off if the day total is correct.
chart: Logged intake versus estimated daily expenditure, seven days ending on the selected day
chartNote: Colored bars are intake; gray bars are estimated expenditure, not Fitbit burn. Intake is blue below 90% of the target, green at 90–110%, and orange above 110%. The line is your current calorie target. Today’s intake is still running. Gaps are unknown.
chartKey: Intake · gray expenditure · dashed current target
historyNote: The chart ends on the selected day. Today’s totals are still updating. Dashed line: current target. Missing values are gaps.
averagesNote: Each graph point averages usable calorie logs in the seven calendar days ending on that date. The graph ends before the selected day. Missing or reviewed incomplete days are omitted, not zero. Macro bars show each nutrient’s known-day average against your current daily target, over the selected 7 or 30 days before that day. All bars use a 0–150% scale: ticks mark the target, and an arrow marks values beyond the scale. Exact grams remain visible. Food log coverage counts days with usable calories, not days you met a target, proof that every meal was logged, or complete macro data.
macroAverageA11y: {{label}}: average {{value}} g per known day; current daily target {{target}} g.
macroMissingA11y: {{label}}: no data for this period; current daily target {{target}} g.
logCoverageA11y: {{days}} of {{span}} days with usable calorie logs, {{from}} to {{to}}. Not a count of days you met your targets or confirmation that every meal was logged.
weightHistoryNote: Dots mark weigh-in days; the line connects smoothed estimates. Missing days aren’t measurements.
weightNote: Weight uses a seven-day exponential half-life. Values and changes follow your chosen units. The trend can move with water, not just fat. After seven days without a weigh-in, its current value is withheld.
planNote: The original plan starts {{day}} and stays fixed as your estimates or calorie target change. A difference is a prompt to review water changes, activity and logs, not proof of under-reporting.
planNeeds: Needs calibration, a target and today’s weigh-in.
planRequirements: Choose your calorie target, finish calibration and record a weigh-in today to save an original plan. Future progress is compared with that fixed starting estimate.
netChart: Daily net energy comparison. Left blue bars subtract intake/weight-estimated whole-day expenditure from intake; right gray bars subtract estimated BMR plus wearable-reported active calories. Faded blue bars with a tilde are provisional, low-confidence estimates during calibration. Negative is deficit, positive is surplus. Missing or unfinished food days have no bars.
netDayA11y: {{day}}: {{status}}. Calculated {{calculated}} kcal net, {{estimate}}; wearable {{wearable}} kcal net

netStatus.ongoing: Day in progress · daily net withheld

netTrendsNote: Calculated averages use available daily net values in the last 7 or 30 calendar days and compare with the immediately preceding equal-length window. Today is omitted. Coverage is shown for both windows: missing, incomplete or uncalibrated days are not zero. A change between sparse windows may not represent a true trend. Provisional means either window contains early, low-confidence expenditure estimates; later calibration never backfills earlier days.
goalHint: Optional · blank removes the goal. Does not change your calorie budget.

goalState.unset: Set a goal for a rough time estimate
goalState.needWeights: More weigh-in history needed for an ETA
goalState.reached: Weight trend is at your goal
goalState.steady: Weight trend is steady · no ETA yet
goalState.away: Trend is moving away from goal · no ETA

goalNote: A rough straight-line projection of your smoothed weight trend, not a prediction from a single day's deficit or a promised date. Needs at least 3 weigh-ins spanning 14 days in the last 28 days, with the latest at most 7 days old. It uses the change between the earliest and latest smoothed weigh-in values in that window. Near-flat trends (less than 0.05 kg/week), stale data and trends moving away from the goal get no ETA. Within 0.1 kg counts as at goal. Estimates round up to weeks and show more than a year beyond 52 weeks. Water changes, illness and future habits can change the pace. Goal weight is saved only on this phone and never changes your calorie target or original plan.
exerciseMethods:
HR {{hr}} · activity MET {{met}} min
Wearable {{wearable}} · uncovered {{uncovered}} min
hrAudit: HR present {{covered}} min. Outside HR equation: exercise type {{type}}, HR range {{range}}, missing HR {{missing}}, profile {{profile}} min. Other methods may cover these minutes.
netCaveat: Calculated uses intake + weight, not HR exercise calories. Provisional values can shift with water weight and logging errors. Wearable uses estimated BMR + Health Connect active calories. Never extra food allowance.
netNote: Net is intake minus daily expenditure: negative means deficit; positive means surplus. The blue left bar uses a causal whole-day intake/weight expenditure estimate, using only that day and earlier data. Full calibration needs at least 7 weigh-ins spanning 14 days within a rolling 28-day window, with a weigh-in in the last 7 days. During initial calibration, an early fit can appear after at least 2 weigh-ins spanning 7 days of usable intake. This is a display guard, not a guarantee of accuracy. It is labelled Provisional · low confidence and drawn faded with a tilde. Water changes and food-logging errors can move it substantially. It never changes the calibrated baseline, calorie targets, remaining food, Energy balance's calibrated expenditure bars or the original plan. Without enough early data, after a food gap or with a weigh-in more than 7 days old, it stays unavailable. A held calibrated estimate is not substituted for fresh net. BMR and exercise HR are not required for calculated net, and neither is added to expenditure. The gray right bar instead subtracts estimated BMR plus Health Connect ActiveCaloriesBurned (Fitbit when it supplies them), never TotalCaloriesBurned plus BMR. Source provenance is not retained in the daily aggregate, so a Fitbit-exclusive origin cannot be guaranteed. BMR is a Mifflin–St Jeor resting-energy estimate (1990, doi:10.1093/ajcn/51.2.241), in kcal per 24 hours, from sex, height, age 19–78 and the latest weight on or before that day, at most 30 days old. It is not measured BMR. Neither series is a measurement of actual daily expenditure. Today, missing intake and incomplete food logs have no net bars. Missing-energy detection marks a log incomplete automatically; turning off Incomplete food log confirms the known daily total for both comparisons. Missing inputs stay unknown, not zero; an explicitly reported zero is retained. HR-modeled exercise remains a separate coverage-limited metric.
activityNote: Coverage-limited exercise estimate · never extra food calories
hrNote: Exercise estimates combine non-overlapping methods, in order: eligible steady-cardio HR (Keytel 2005, 90–150 bpm, ages 18–45, weights 47–120 kg); coarse activity METs for named racket/team sports, strength, yoga and other supported activities (2024 Adult Compendium, general/moderate effort, ages 19–59, weight required); then wearable calories for remaining minutes. Generic Racket sports or Activity does not identify a sport, so it follows the wearable rather than guessing a MET. Only minute-or-finer calorie records count: total calories are used at 1×; active-only calories get estimated 1-MET resting energy added so all methods include rest during exercise. Overlapping workouts and devices are never added together. Gaps and coarse daily/hourly totals remain uncovered, not zero. These are provisional population/device estimates, not personally calibrated exercise calories, whole-day expenditure or extra food allowance. They never change calculated daily net or your calorie target.
wearableNote: Health Connect’s reported total, shown for comparison only. Today’s total is incomplete.
targetHint: Match the calorie budget you use in Lose It! Blank uses the maintenance reference. Exercise never adds a bonus.
maintenanceBasis: Maintenance inferred from intake and weight; not a chosen weight-loss target
referenceBasis: 2,000 kcal food-label reference, not a personalized estimate. Set your own target.
proteinHeight: Based on a healthy weight for {{height}} {{heightUnit}} ({{weight}} {{unit}}). Log your weight to use yours.
